sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: 46 Exploring Society: India and Beyond | Grade 7 Part 1 Weather, Seasons and the Climate ‘Climate’ is a word people use in everyday conversations.
sections.source_evidence: 46 Exploring Society: India and Beyond | Grade 7 Part 1 Weather, Seasons and the Climate ‘Climate’ is a word people use in everyday conversations.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: But, quite often, what they really mean is ‘weather’, and not ‘climate’.
sections.source_evidence: But, quite often, what they really mean is ‘weather’, and not ‘climate’.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: ‘Weather’ is what we experience every hour or day: it might be raining, or there could be bright sunshine, a lot of wind, etc.
sections.source_evidence: ‘Weather’ is what we experience every hour or day: it might be raining, or there could be bright sunshine, a lot of wind, etc.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: Climate, on the other hand, is the pattern of weather an area or a region experiences over a long period of time — several decades at least.
sections.source_evidence: Climate, on the other hand, is the pattern of weather an area or a region experiences over a long period of time — several decades at least.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: This pattern varies from region to region.
sections.source_evidence: This pattern varies from region to region.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: Before we come to the various types of climates, let us briefly stop to introduce seasons.
sections.source_evidence: Before we come to the various types of climates, let us briefly stop to introduce seasons.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: Seasons occur as the Earth revolves around the Sun.
sections.source_evidence: Seasons occur as the Earth revolves around the Sun.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: Each season lasts for a few months and recurs every year.
sections.source_evidence: Each season lasts for a few months and recurs every year.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: As we know, there are several seasons in the year — spring, summer, monsoon, autumn and winter — that occur in a cycle.
sections.source_evidence: As we know, there are several seasons in the year — spring, summer, monsoon, autumn and winter — that occur in a cycle.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: Are seasons related to the weather or to the climate?
sections.source_evidence: Are seasons related to the weather or to the climate?

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: The weather changes with the season, that is, it can be dry and hot in the summer months, or humid and rainy during the monsoon.
sections.source_evidence: The weather changes with the season, that is, it can be dry and hot in the summer months, or humid and rainy during the monsoon.

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: Further, the pattern of seasons in a region is closely connected with the climate.
sections.source_evidence: Further, the pattern of seasons in a region is closely connected with the climate.

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: There are four main seasons across most regions of the world — spring, summer, autumn and winter.
sections.source_evidence: There are four main seasons across most regions of the world — spring, summer, autumn and winter.

sections.heading: Learning Point 18
sections.content: However, India receives rainfall during a specific period of the year — the ‘rainy season’ or monsoon — along with the other four.
sections.source_evidence: However, India receives rainfall during a specific period of the year — the ‘rainy season’ or monsoon — along with the other four.

sections.heading: Learning Point 19
sections.content: Traditionally, in many parts of India, the year is divided into six seasons or ṛitus — vasanta (spring), grīṣhma (summer), varṣhā (rainy season), śharad (autumn), hemanta (pre-winter), śhiśhir (winter).
sections.source_evidence: Traditionally, in many parts of India, the year is divided into six seasons or ṛitus — vasanta (spring), grīṣhma (summer), varṣhā (rainy season), śharad (autumn), hemanta (pre-winter), śhiśhir (winter).

sections.heading: Learning Point 20
sections.content: Specific rituals and festivals are associated with these six ṛitus, such as Vasanta Pañchamī or Śharad Pūrṇima.
sections.source_evidence: Specific rituals and festivals are associated with these six ṛitus, such as Vasanta Pañchamī or Śharad Pūrṇima.
